correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\) and admissible \(m\), conditioning on the training mean gives exact null expectation one. Under \(N(\mu,1)\), independence yields \(\mathbb E[\widehat\mu\overline Y_0]=\mu^2\) and \(\mathbb E[\widehat\mu^2]=\mu^2+1/m\), proving the e-power formula. The forward difference is exactly \(\frac12[n/(m(m+1))-\mu^2]\), which is strictly decreasing in \(m\) and proves the integer optimizer and tie cases. The local and fixed-signal limits follow from this threshold characterization. A standalone verifier brute-checks the finite integer characterization and asymptotic examples.

value.rationale: Split-ratio tuning is an explicit practical and theoretical issue in universal inference. The exact law exposes a substantive criterion conflict: e-power-optimal splitting can use a vanishing training fraction for fixed alternatives even though published rejection-power and confidence-radius criteria generally favor nonvanishing fractions. The local \(|h|=1\) phase gives a sharp detectability boundary for positive expected log growth. This is a natural design invariant of a widely studied procedure rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
